rows.description: I scored the winning point and a teammate goes quiet and sulks. I understand he wanted that chance. I credit his pass and include him. Downplaying myself completely is not needed either.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, pride

rows.description: I could bend the rule and nobody would notice. Winning feels big and losing feels small. A wise child knows a win by cheating feels empty and would need to be hidden. I play fair.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, guilt

rows.description: I cheated and won, and the trophy feels heavy. Guilt is my conscience working. I can admit it to the coach, accept a consequence and start clean. Hiding it makes it grow.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, temptation

rows.description: I catch someone cheating against me and feel furious. Wise: tell the referee or an adult calmly instead of accusing loudly or retaliating. Cheating back turns me into the same thing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: guilt, temptation

rows.description: I did most of the project while others chatted and I am fuming. Resentment is fair, but silent martyrdom fixes nothing. Wise: ask clearly for tasks to be split, and tell the teacher if it continues.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, gratitude, rejection

rows.description: I let others do the work because I think they will do it anyway. It feels easy but it takes advantage. Honest action: take a real share and admit when I have been slack.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, gratitude, rejection, resentment

rows.description: I take over the project because I think only my way is right. My ideas may be good, but others feel shut out. Wise: listen, give each person a part, and accept some imperfection.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, gratitude, rejection, resentment

rows.description: My group gives me only tiny jobs and ignores my ideas. I feel small. I can speak up calmly with an idea and ask for a bigger role. If still ignored, I tell the teacher without being harsh.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, gratitude, resentment

rows.description: A group mate stayed late to fix my part and did not complain. I feel grateful and a little guilty. I say thank you clearly and do my share next time. Thankless taking sours teams.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, rejection, resentment

rows.description: I ask the teacher to see who did what. Asking for fairness is not tale-telling. Wise: describe facts calmly, not blame. Wanting all the credit for myself is a different thing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude, rejection, resentment
